summary: Full e2e testing of Twenty20 Wariyad Charity Management Platform. All 31 backend API tests passed. Frontend UI loads, login works, all 9 pages navigate correctly, Add Member form works (member added with auto-generated TW-001 ID), logout redirects to login page.

ui_bugs.issue: Form input fields (Full Name, Mobile, Address) do not have individual data-testid attributes, making automated testing harder. Inputs can only be selected by nth-child position.

issues: Joining Date displays as '10/6/2026' - inconsistent date format (should be consistent with input format '2026-06-10' or '10 Jun 2026')

action_items: Add individual data-testid attributes to form inputs in Add Member modal (name-input, mobile-input, address-input, joining-date-input) for better testability
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: next_member_id() uses count_documents({}) - if a member is deleted, the count decreases and next ID could collide with existing IDs. Should use a sequence or find the max existing ID instead.
server.py: CORS allows only FRONTEND_URL but also has CORS_ORIGINS='*' in .env which is unused - minor inconsistency.
server.py: Cookie samesite='lax' with secure=False - for production, secure should be True when served over HTTPS.
Members.jsx: Modal form inputs missing data-testid attributes for individual fields.

success_rate.frontend: 95% - all pages load, login/logout works, add member works, all nav links work

seed_data_creation: Created and cleaned up TEST_ prefixed members/contributions/benefits via backend tests. One 'UI Test Member' (TW-001) remains from frontend testing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend: 31/31 tests pass. Frontend: All pages load and navigate correctly. Add Member form works (fills name/mobile via nth locator, address via textarea locator). Logout redirects to /login. The contribution-status-table data-testid was not found during quick check - needs re-verification with actual members in DB.
rca_of_issues: Member ID generation race condition: next_member_id() counts documents which could give duplicate IDs if members are deleted. Example: if TW-001 exists and TW-002 is deleted, next ID would be TW-002 again - valid but potentially confusing. Minor data integrity concern.
